notes.title: Dev Blog #19 - Last content update before full release!
notes.content:
Hi there, Lightbringers! 

It’s been some time since the last dev blog, but we haven’t been idle at Poleaxe Games, and, as the end of the last milestone approached, we’ve been working tirelessly to finish the last level of the game.

And finally... after almost four years in development and eight months on Early Access, we’re proud to announce that we’ve implemented the LAST UPDATE that completes the main storyline of [i]Empire of Ember[/i]! HURRAAAY!!! 🥳🎉🎉🎉

In this last level, our Lightbringer hero will at last confront the forces that endanger the world in a final battle... but we don’t want major spoilers, so we’re only leaving you this image 😉

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/cc0104da414808fad9c289d815edf508dcb3f2da.jpg[/img]

So these are the exciting news we wanted to share with you!!! 

Now that the game is content complete, we will focus on testing and polishing ahead of the final release of the game. You can follow up our progress with the final touches on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/wBjX9jEWTY][b]Discord[/b][/url] server, and our Social Media channels, [url=https://twitter.com/PoleaxeG][b]Twitter[/b][/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/Empire-of-Ember-101973105217165][b]Facebook[/b][/url] and [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/empireofember/][b]Reddit[/b][/url].

As always, thank you all for your feedback on the game! If you haven’t already, please remember to leave us a [b]review[/b] on Steam, update your old review, or [b]rate[/b] existing reviews that you think would be useful for other users.

Also, [b]wishlist and follow[/b] [i]Empire of Ember[/i] on Steam, and spread the news 😊

Have a great week!

notes.title: Dev Blog #17 - Tips, controls and strategy (Part II)
notes.content:
Hello again, Lightbringers! 

Last week we shared with you a few tricks and tips to help you better understand the controls in the game and know your stuff to make the most out of [i]Empire of Ember[/i] ([url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/980640/view/2869346378552865060][b]check it out here[/b][/url] if you missed it!). 

So here you are a few more! Using these at the right time can save your day.


[h5]ARMY MANAGEMENT[/h5]

[list]
[*] New recruits are drawn from your population resource. Increase the number of units you can bring in your army by leveling up, training leadership, or building farms. Also, find and help villages in order to recruit idle villagers, otherwise you will eventually run out of men!

[*] Assign unit loadouts on the army management screen. Blunt weapons are good general-purpose weapons while slash weapons are good against living units. Heavy shields provide more protection but result in slow movement and slow stamina recovery.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/a82f84475252cef466ab4d85897918933198fa97.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Non-undead units left behind to train will gain a small amount of XP per day. Eventually a plus sign will appear and you can pay to level them to a better unit. You can level up your army faster with the training enchantment, but only units that survive will benefit.

[*] If you are concerned about your city coming under siege, try recruiting extra units to leave behind in the garrison. You will be defeated if enemies are successful in destroying your wizard tower, or if you are knocked out too many times during a siege battle. Strength in numbers! 
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/97fe369f1357f9b37cda87140983fb8c5ac0b9e5.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] The leadership attribute lets you save units from death, ready to fight again the next battle. This can be helpful for recruiting high-level armies at low cost.
[/list]

[h5]KNOW YOUR ENEMY[/h5]

[list]
[*] At higher difficulty levels enemies build up their strength based on days passed, becoming more aggressive, higher level, and appearing in larger numbers.

[*] Also at higher difficulties, enemies may steal your equipment if you are defeated. If applicable, you may cast the contingency enchantment before resting in your tower to prevent this.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/9973b5bfd481507b663916fa1d7cfcba59ea0857.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] Enemies that are aware of you will constantly shout, alerting their nearby allies.

[*] You can usually recover lost equipment by defeating the enemies who took it from you.
[/list]

[h5]BUFF![/h5]

[list]
[*] Berzerk increases damage, attack speed, and move speed. However, your indiscriminate attacks also fully damage allies.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/637f01053cad547744d7f0d2320d1d24f820f013.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Enhance your equipment further with set bonuses, by equipping multiple rings that provide the same benefit.
[/list]

[h5]SPELLS[/h5]

[list]
[*] Casting spells tires you out, inflicting mana burn. This reduces how much mana you have for the rest of the level.

[*] If you see a purple crystal while inside your wizard tower, this means you have enough ember to research or upgrade a spell.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/a29a1d670d691ae628dcc3bbc44499a02ac696a7.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Basic mana bolts from your staff apply a slight slow status on enemies, which can be used for defense or to bunch up enemies.

[*] Single out enemies in a melee with chain lightning. It will jump between nearby enemy targets.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/44813ab36dc35084ac0a1eff6a921bfc97960e63.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Entropy does not just break objects, it explodes them. Try using breakable objects as traps.

[*] Upgrade your telekinesis spell to pull weapons from enemy hands. However this won't work against bosses or enemies that do not carry weapons.

[*] While carrying an object with telekinesis, right click (default) to cancel the spell and place the object on the ground, at no mana cost. This can be used to setup traps.

[*] Telekinesis can pick up knocked down enemies, which can be used for a variety of purposes.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/9aafc6a07b7620504115329f6b897193b1602b7f.gif[/img]

[h5]ECONOMY AND CITY MANAGEMENT[/h5]

[list]
[*] Build multiple markets to increase how many goods are available for purchase each day.

[*] Sell gems and unwanted items at villages, or by building a market.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/800de3a069636f9ed8fc79770e34383ca1251164.gif[/img]

[h5]THE DUNGEON SECRETS[/h5]

[list]
[*] Search carefully while in dungeons. You may find secret rooms!

[*] Deeper levels of dungeons sometimes have rooms where you can rest and recover health.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/fefa8265d9e5cb5f9b5dea6d3a25175dd21d75d4.jpg[/img]

This will be all for now! If you know any other tricks or tips you’d like to share with the community, please do so on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/wBjX9jEWTY][b]Discord[/b][/url] server, [b]Steam[/b] hub, or our Social Media channels, [url=https://twitter.com/PoleaxeG][b]Twitter[/b][/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/Empire-of-Ember-101973105217165][b]Facebook[/b][/url] and [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/empireofember/][b]Reddit[/b][/url]!

We’d also love to hear your feedback about the game! Leave us a [b]review on Steam[/b], or [b]update your old review[/b] -the game keeps changing and improving thanks to your comments!-, and [b]rate other reviews[/b] if you find them useful ːsteamthumbsupː

[b]Wishlist and follow [i]Empire of Ember[/i] on Steam[/b], and tell all your friends about it!

Have a great week, and see you soon!

notes.title: Dev Blog #16 - Tips, controls and strategy (Part I)
notes.content:
Welcome back, Lightbringers! 

Here we are one more week! We’ve been listening to your feedback and it seems that new players as well as a few more experienced players sometimes struggle with the game controls. This issue has been addressed by further improving the starting tutorial of the game by making changes that better explain how basic controls work, the different types of melee attacks, attack direction switching, and more details about staff combat. Furthermore, the build-mode has been simplified and made a lot more user-friendly, with a new option being added to the general tab to switch between full controls and the simplified ones.

In this dev blog, we would like to refresh some of the useful game controls and give you a few tips that will come in handy, especially for combat. Here we go!


[h5]SOME BASIC CONTROLS[/h5]

[list]
[*] Hold down [b]SHIFT[/b] while moving to run. Physical activities such as jumping, dodging, or running use stamina. When you run out of it, you’ll be slowed down, so be careful. The quick footed ability lets you run using less stamina, which is useful to flee from battles.

[*] With melee weapons, hold down the [b]left mouse button to perform a power attack[/b]. The directional indicator will follow the direction you are looking to show which direction your next swing will occur in.
[/list]⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/402442326f93e7ace5d3d320790eba4838cb7ffd.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] With wands and staves, use the [b]left mouse button to fire[/b], [b]middle button to recharge[/b]. While fully loaded, your magic weapons will build up charges over time, for greater area of effect and damage.

[*] Press [b]Q[/b] on keyboard or [b]right stick down[/b] on the gamepad [b]to zoom[/b] in and see further.
[/list]⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/20420907ceae829d02147d5f7f0431c00cee2ef8.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Get a [b]better view of the minimap[/b] using default [b]E[/b] on the keyboard or [b]left stick down[/b] on the gamepad.

[*] Enable detailed health bars in options to view friendly and/or enemy stamina (yellow) and poise (green).

[*] Press [b]ALT to dodge[/b]. This can be used with any weapon. Dodging depends on stamina; however, you can still dodge even without having sufficient stamina, but not as far. Increasing athleticism makes it cheaper to dodge.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/15f2130dfc715fdeeb0fdd3711d731cc50d8b8bd.gif[/img]

[h5]GET A GOOD REST[/h5]

[list]
[*] Recover mana quickly without sprinting, attacking, or taking damage for a few seconds.
[/list]

[h5]THE POWER OF ARROWS[/h5]

[list]
[*] When using the bow, try shooting the head, leg, or arm. These shots apply greater damage, knockdown, or weapon drop effects respectively on enemies if enough damage was done to one those limbs.
[/list]
⠀⠀⠀⠀
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/0e26178421912956a94422ccd5c5331e2a700e9b.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] If you wait until the reticle changes color your shot will do additional damage. Shooting when the reticle changes colour invokes a power attack for additional damage. 

[*] Pierce damage will not do much harm to skeletons.
[/list]

[h5]PROBLEMS WITH A MISSION?[/h5]

[list]
[*] If you are having trouble with an army battle, try leveling up peasants with easier fights. You can leave behind stronger units in your garrison, undergoing training, where they gain experience automatically while upkeep costs are reduced.

[*] Alchemy gives expensive but powerful enchantments. Try it out if you are having trouble with a particular mission.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/dc2d69cbacfaa2ff145729e6d706913ca4f1c7e7.jpg[/img]

[h5]OUTNUMBERED?[/h5]

[list]
[*] Be sure to bring crowd control spells, especially if you are not carrying a melee weapon.

[*] Enemies aggro to those who damaged them, so if you have trouble with foes ganging up on you, just limit your damage to one of them at a time or wait until that enemy is engaged.

[*] A retreat in time is a victory, run away if you are going to lose a battle. You can always come back and fight later, avoiding the penalties associated with being defeated.
[/list]

[h5]MASTER OF THE WEAPONS[/h5]

[list]
[*] Research the passive ability Weapon Master to carry multiple weapons into battle. Press [b]TAB[/b] to switch weapons. Also, the finesse ability lets you change weapons faster. 
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/39916ec9e5b1a7b682960f22c635799536e21514.jpg[/img]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/fad6ca27255e1603a69b1ecd255fe2c1758e97f9.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] When using a melee weapon, block at the last moment to perform a perfect block. This will cause the enemy to recoil longer, and not reduce your poise.
[/list]

[h5]SIMPLIFIED BUILD MODE[/h5]

[list]
[*] The build mode tutorial will now prompt between simplified and full controls, and a new option has been added to the general tab of the options screen to switch between those modes. The simplified build mode allows placing buildings with a single click, so if you are not really into city decoration, it’s worth checking it out. It can be accessed through the options screen in the general tab. 
[/list]

[h5]WHERE TO GET RESOURCES[/h5]

Most resources used in construction can be found by destroying items and buildings you will find in cities, villages and dungeons, and can appear as random loot. You can also get both raw and refined materials trading in the market or buying them from other villages. 

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/6077dfa1a2d5a8cb4c60133c1c60c15872555bc8.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Stone: Necessary to fortify higher level walls and stronger buildings. It is also used as ammunition for the catapult.
[*] Wood/Timber: Raw wood. Build a sawmill and use it to produce lumber.
[*] Lumber: Used in construction. Sawmills produce lumber from timber.
[*] Ore: Can be refined into steel at a blacksmith. 
[*] Steel: It is used to recruit and maintain units. You can obtain it from a blacksmith using steel ore.
[*] Spellbooks: Used to research higher level buildings and units. You can get them by exploring dungeons and building libraries.
[/list]

notes.title: Added basic modding support
notes.content:
[b]Basic modding support:[/b]
Per request from [b]anduril38 [/b] users can now override various numbers used in the game, such as player or enemy health. To do so, find D:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Empire of Ember\Empire of Ember_Data\StreamingAssets or your equivalent directory. In that directory you'll find json and CSV files that define numbers used by the game. Create a new file with the same name and a suffix, and the same file extension to override that file. For example, if you create a file named Difficulty_Easy_Override1.json values in that JSON will override any default game settings, or any game settings from the easy difficulty. Difficulty_Default_Override1.json would override game settings on any difficulty. Units_Default_Override1.csv would override AI settings on any difficulty. This file can be opened in excel. 

Default values can be found in Difficulty_Default.json and Units_Default.csv
For example, to add more starting player health at all difficulties the contents of Difficulty_Default_Override1.json would be 
{
 "items": [
 {
  "key": "AvatarHealth_Starting",
  "value": 100
 }
 ]
}

For Units_Default_Override1.csv it's easiest to start with Units_Medium.csv and rename it because the columns and rows are already setup. You can then just fill in entries you want to override and leave blank the ones you do not. 

[b]Further Improved Tutorial[/b]
I had a third party testing company help me find bugs, and also have each of those players write a report on their experiences. The most common theme was they didn't understand the game. Either it was too hard because they didn't know how to do something the game actually could do, or they asked for features that was already there. To improve this the tutorial is further improved, explaining the different types of melee attacks, attack direction switching, and more details about staff combat.

Still to-do is add a more interactive commander mode to show players the value of controlling their units.

In addition, new games start with all 3 weapons rather than having the player choose a starting weapon. This way if a player doesn't like one weapon type they can more easily choose another, without having to know to build a market.

[b]Other improvements:[/b]
[list]
[*] The player can now shoot enemies who are in ragdoll on the ground using the bow
[*] Enemy reactions to being blocked now last 15% longer
[*] Increase mana bolt damage 15%
[/list]

notes.title: Dev Blog #13 – A quick catch up… 6 months later
notes.content:
Greetings, Lightbringers!

Time flies, it’s been almost six months since [i]Empire of Ember[/i] hit Early Access! This week we would like to run a retrospective to see how much the game has improved in this time.

Having [i]Empire of Ember[/i] released on Early Access has allowed the community to try the game as it develops and has also provided us an opportunity to take stock of all the feedback provided- both positive and negative-, allowing us to continue working and improving the game.

The full release of [i]Empire of Ember[/i] is initially intended within Q1 2022, but of course, this is not written in stone. Any game development cannot be 100% accurately planned, as this is subject to balancing all the feedback and improvements we want to make to deliver the best and most enjoyable gaming experience we possibly can to our players.

Since the Early Access release, there has been a considerable restructuring of the initial build. Here are some of the most relevant changes compared to six months ago:
 

[h3]GENERAL [/h3]
[list]
[*] Framerate has been doubled on most missions and even in the most complex battles should stay above 40 FPS.
[*] Load times have been cut roughly in half, including startup and shutdown.
[*] The game now runs better on very low-end systems, including the ability to use forward instead of deferred rendering.
[*] Sounds for the entire game have been redone.
[*] The visuals for most levels have been improved, with better textures for player buildings.
[*] Difficulty levels have been implemented. Per user request, medium difficulty no longer increases game difficulty based on time.
[*] Better-looking terrain with a new terrain rendering system.
[*] Gamepad should now work consistently.
[*] Enemies should no longer move through walls when getting up.
[*] The female avatar has an all-new cloth system, for better visuals when her sleeves move.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/ee7679299564310e7d4461b539140c1e1ef467a9.gif[/img]

[h3]COMBAT[/h3]
[list]
[*] The player has all-new combat animations.
[*] Player's melee combat has been reworked, allowing for attacks from multiple directions that enemies attempt to parry. Blocking feels more consistent and responsive. The player also has a new shove ability, to push enemies into spikes or get around shielded enemies.
[*] Units now fall into archetypes, adding a strategy element to your army composition. For example, one teleporting ghost may be able to defeat an entire army of melee units by himself, while presenting no challenge to even a single archer.
[*] Commander mode was greatly improved, allowing better unit selection while avoiding unintended orders.
[*] Players having trouble with certain missions can now take advantage of the new alchemy system, allowing the player to spend spellbooks in order to give big bonuses to combat, including regenerating health, a much-requested feature.
[*] Troops can be directly given commands using the function keys, instead of the radial wheel, allowing for faster and more accurate commands without having to leave combat. Gamepad users have a radial wheel alternative.
[*] Catapults now use stone to shoot, preventing exploiting this otherwise too powerful unit.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/e18e07c12436537d23ad281c267cd8a7270f7519.gif[/img]
 
[h3]ENEMIES[/h3]
[list]
[*] Enemies now drop gems of varying rarity after combat, which can be sold at a high price.
[*] Enemies should seem much smarter now. They follow formations and commands better while being less likely to be stuck or confused.
[*] Enemy aggro has been improved, such that enemies will attack the player when he is a threat, but not overwhelm the player and deaggro when attacked by the player's allies. A new spell 'Harmless' was also added to allow users to directly deaggro or even charm enemies when upgraded.
[*] Enemy armies on the campaign map now present a broad range of challenges rather than being consistently difficulty. This gives the player an opportunity to recover from previous losses.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/90c853b0549fa56fb3c245c1af44c47f3e1e6e99.png[/img]
 
[h3]SPELLS[/h3]
[list]
[*] Telekinesis now shows a path indicator, so players can target distant enemies consistently.
[*] New spell 'magelight' used to lead the player through the darkness.
[*] The 'entropy' and 'loot magnet' spells were added, to help players that like to destroy everything.
[/list]
 
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/dd332b84ced55ad75f9c2110fd5f1a655fc0fc5a.gif[/img]

[h3]MANAGEMENT & ATTRIBUTES[/h3]
 [list]
[*] The economy has been rebalanced, where players now get raw resources from villages which they process in their own city. Steel is used for units, spellbooks for research, and wood for buildings.
[*] Each of the player's attributes now plays a big role in the game, allowing for different play styles. For example, athletics allows for faster running, more dodging, and faster bow firing allowing the player to kite enemies more easily. Meanwhile, weaponry increases damage overall and melee attack speed in particular, suitable for a DPS-focused player.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/8b8021421854a1d6ad8d03b878d6ddfdd70449e4.png[/img] 
 
[h3]CONTENT[/h3]
 [list]
[*] Cities have been added. Cities have their own missions, which pay well and also increase the player's reputation with that city. However, most missions reduce reputation with some other cities, leading them to attack you. This has been tied into the online city sharing feature, meaning every city siege is different.
[*] A dynamic day/night system was added, with a new spell 'magelight' used to lead the player through the darkness.
[*] The game has been made more accessible for new players, with a better tutorial that makes clear the early game mechanics.
[*] A whole new research system has been added, a dice-roll minigame that gives increasing rewards at higher levels, including unlocking units or discovering equipment.
[*] Most dialogues have been reviewed and improved by a new writer, Scott Hamm, who also worked on the Age of Decadence and Battle Brothers series of games.
[/list]

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/91d104ad806950f1980b51d205e01953b1c7dcbb.gif[/img]

The current roadmap will now focus on tracking and fixing bugs and improving combat, performance, and other technical aspects. We continue to work hard on adding to the above to provide a top-notch game experience to all our players!

In these past few months, the dev team has been working day and night to address all the issues spotted by the community. A huge thanks to all of you, your feedback has been crucial for the game to feel as it is now, and will continue to help it grow in the right direction!

tags.feature: Framerate has been doubled on most missions and even in the most complex battles should stay above 40 FPS.
Load times have been cut roughly in half, including startup and shutdown.
The game now runs better on very low-end systems, including the ability to use forward instead of deferred rendering.
Sounds for the entire game have been redone.
The visuals for most levels have been improved, with better textures for player buildings.
Difficulty levels have been implemented. Per user request, medium difficulty no longer increases game difficulty based on time.
Better-looking terrain with a new terrain rendering system.

tags.bug: Gamepad should now work consistently.
Enemies should no longer move through walls when getting up.

tags.feature: The female avatar has an all-new cloth system, for better visuals when her sleeves move.
The player has all-new combat animations.

Player's melee combat has been reworked, allowing for attacks from multiple directions that enemies attempt to parry. Blocking feels more consistent and responsive. The player also has a new shove ability, to push enemies into spikes or get around shielded enemies.

Units now fall into archetypes, adding a strategy element to your army composition. For example, one teleporting ghost may be able to defeat an entire army of melee units by himself, while presenting no challenge to even a single archer.
Commander mode was greatly improved, allowing better unit selection while avoiding unintended orders.

Players having trouble with certain missions can now take advantage of the new alchemy system, allowing the player to spend spellbooks in order to give big bonuses to combat, including regenerating health, a much-requested feature.

Troops can be directly given commands using the function keys, instead of the radial wheel, allowing for faster and more accurate commands without having to leave combat. Gamepad users have a radial wheel alternative.

tags.balance_change: Catapults now use stone to shoot, preventing exploiting this otherwise too powerful unit.

tags.feature: Enemies now drop gems of varying rarity after combat, which can be sold at a high price.
Enemies should seem much smarter now. They follow formations and commands better while being less likely to be stuck or confused.

Enemy aggro has been improved, such that enemies will attack the player when he is a threat, but not overwhelm the player and deaggro when attacked by the player's allies. A new spell 'Harmless' was also added to allow users to directly deaggro or even charm enemies when upgraded.
Enemy armies on the campaign map now present a broad range of challenges rather than being consistently difficulty. This gives the player an opportunity to recover from previous losses.
Telekinesis now shows a path indicator, so players can target distant enemies consistently.
New spell 'magelight' used to lead the player through the darkness.
The 'entropy' and 'loot magnet' spells were added, to help players that like to destroy everything.

tags.balance_change: The economy has been rebalanced, where players now get raw resources from villages which they process in their own city. Steel is used for units, spellbooks for research, and wood for buildings.

tags.feature: Each of the player's attributes now plays a big role in the game, allowing for different play styles. For example, athletics allows for faster running, more dodging, and faster bow firing allowing the player to kite enemies more easily. Meanwhile, weaponry increases damage overall and melee attack speed in particular, suitable for a DPS-focused player.

Cities have been added. Cities have their own missions, which pay well and also increase the player's reputation with that city. However, most missions reduce reputation with some other cities, leading them to attack you. This has been tied into the online city sharing feature, meaning every city siege is different.
A dynamic day/night system was added, with a new spell 'magelight' used to lead the player through the darkness.
The game has been made more accessible for new players, with a better tutorial that makes clear the early game mechanics.
A whole new research system has been added, a dice-roll minigame that gives increasing rewards at higher levels, including unlocking units or discovering equipment.
Most dialogues have been reviewed and improved by a new writer, Scott Hamm, who also worked on the Age of Decadence and Battle Brothers series of games.

notes.title: New player introduction patch
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Enemy lairs and hordes close to your base now have far fewer enemies, while those far away have slightly more. This gives the player easier fight options if they need it.
[*] At the start of the game, you will encounter roaming pitchfork farmer hordes in addition to the other horde types (such as goblins) since peasants are pretty easy to mow down. However, they give less gold per kill.
[*] Pitchfork farmers now do much more damage, attack more often, and have slightly more health allowing them to be more useful at low levels. This way if the player wipes out it is easier to recover, and also makes them viable combat units and not just fodder.
[*] Player starts with more population at the start of the game, so new players can withstand a few losses without running out.
[*] Higher level units take half as much steel to recruit or upgrade to. This lets the player recover strong armies or individually lost units more easily. It was so expensive before high level units still cost a lot to purchase directly.
[*] Player starts with a larger starting army limit. This reduces difficulty for new players by reducing player aggro, without affecting end-game difficulty.
[*] The player now does slightly less melee damage to account for the greater attack speed vs. other weapons. Previously the player was able to kill the majority of enemies by himself.
[*] Horde and lair battles now give more experience, making an under-leveled player able to grind them and be rewarded even if there are not many enemies.
[*] Add gameplay tab option to disable screen turning grey at player low health.
[/list]

notes.title: Dev Blog #9 - The first animation patch for Empire of Ember has been released!
notes.content:
Hi there, Lightbringers! 

In this week’s dev blog we are pleased to announce that the first animation patch for [i]Empire of Ember[/i] has finally been implemented in the game! 

This first pass includes improved first-person animations for the different styles of combat; that is, melee, bow, spell and staff attacks. 

These improvements will be most noticeable during melee combat. This should make the animations feel more responsive, cleaner and balanced than before. The main difference now is that players will need to use their reflexes to block attacks in time, or cancel attacks in progress. Melee users will now be able to block with a magical shield, and also have a new unlockable “shove” ability to counteract enemies that are using shields.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/e0ef932ffb4ff9de51366ff3e43d334c18c4e7c1.gif[/img]

Implementing the animations for [i]Empire of Ember[/i] hasn’t been a bed of roses all the time, as there have been some very challenging moments. Most issues have been a consequence of the hired animators not properly testing their work in-game. Even animators with 20 years of experience had trouble copying FBX files from Maya to Unity, or would not know how to use an animation controller, for instance.

This has unfortunately slowed down progress. Improving the game’s animation has taken about four times longer than expected, and has been more expensive than originally planned. On the bright side, all the setbacks have given main developer Kevin Jenkins the chance to make other improvements that resulted in a better outcome and thus, a better game.

Further additions to the animations are planned for the future, but as these are not a pressing concern anymore, the developers will focus on other fixes for the moment. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/f43fb2ed998b0a54a118f060b609478dc3cbc324.png[/img]

Since the Steam Early Access release in late March, the dev team has been working really hard to polish the weakest parts of the game. All feedback from users has been very useful so far to introduce new features as well as helping fix bugs, so we welcome you all to try the game and let us know how it can be further improved. You can have an impact in shaping [i]Empire of Ember[/i] and helping it reach its full potential!

If you would like to help us, please wishlist and follow the game and tell everyone about it! You can also follow our progress by joining our community on [url=https://discord.com/invite/wBjX9jEWTY]Discord[/url], Steam, and our Social Media channels: [url=https://twitter.com/PoleaxeG]Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/Empire-of-Ember-101973105217165]Facebook[/url] and [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/empireofember/]Reddit[/url].

See you soon! Take care and have a great week :)

notes.title: 2 Additional main storyline missions released
notes.content:
[b]Major Changes[/b]
[olist]
[*] Unlock two additional main storyline missions
[*] Major economy change: You get a fixed amount of gold from your wizard tower, with very little coming from markets. Markets produce fewer resources for trade per turn, but multiple can be built to stack the benefits. The purpose is to add decision making to what you build and remove the ability to get infinite gold just by building markets
[*] Load times should be much better now due to not unloading and reloading certain UI scenes every combat.
[*] Entropy now does AOE damage. This changes it from a convenience spell to break objects to a powerful strategic attack spell, where every breakable object can damage enemies
[/olist]

[b]Minor Changes[/b]
[olist]
[*] Fix bad location assignment for hordes spawned from spawn lair
[*] Solo/small group mission quests no longer end immediately when you defeat the boss
[*] Fix solo/small group mission 3 teleporting the player even without touching substantial water. Also fix enemies killing themselves walking into water
[*] Reduce how often AI pop on top of objects when trying to walk around them
[*] Fix skeleton elites not doing damage with their freeze projectiles
[*] Reduce gold cost of directly buying units
[*] Increase chance of roaming hordes to attack player city
[*] Higher level blink spells can be used more often
[*] Reduce suit of armor magic resistance
[*] Fix floor trap trigger to trigger off enemy movement
[*] Enemies will now miss the avatar with ranged weapons if the avatar is dodging
[*] Enemies no longer play hit reactions from weapons that should not cause hit reactions, such as the player's staff. This was causing it too easy to get enemies to drop shields against mana bolts
[*] Mana bolts now shoot more accurately when standing still, and much less accurately when running
[*] Bosses are no longer killed in one hit using thrown objects
[*] Reduce radius of magic missile shot to require more player aim
[*] Increase suit of armor shield size
[*] Increase chance for enemies to dodge ranged attacks
[*] Show market capacity in trade screen
[*] Reduce trade cost of spellbooks
[*] Fix quest generated bosses not having enough health or fall resistance
[*] Add stairs to section in second level boss dungeon room that makes enemy stuck
[*] Reduce staff damage by about 25% and bow damage by about 15%. This is to slow down the player time to kill, giving more meaning to allied units
[*] The mana amulet Fumi's shadow will now eliminate mana burn, rather than increase max mana
[*] City quests have a longer cooldown
[*] xxRaIenXX: Upgrading your farm still provides the benefit of the old farm while the upgrade is in progress
[*] Orgasinator: Zombies now have about half as many hitpoints, but also cost about half as much to recruit. Fixes necromancy too powerful, zombies costing the same as skeleton archers
[/olist]

[b]Upcoming changes[/b]
[list]
[*] Next week: Improve overall visual quality of the game with better shaders and environmental effects
[*] Within about 2 weeks: Marketing should start brining in new players, which should provide more variety for the downloadable city combat feature
[*] Within about 3 weeks: Each city will have a tournament / challenge. If you beat the challenge you can then court the princess.
[*] Over the next month: Improved unit sounds
[*] Within about 2 months: Final mission for the game should be done.
[*] Ongoing over the next several months: Improved player animations, including a revamped combat system. I might release this gradually instead of all at once. If I can find an animator with more availability this will be a lot faster.
[/list]

notes.title: Cities patch
notes.content:
[b]Requested missions available while negative reputation:[/b]
1. (High probability) Pay tribute. A high gold price, restoring your reputation by a certain amount.
2. (Low probability) Ransom from the enemy boss. An unusually difficult random map mission spawns nearby, with a captured villager. At the start of the mission you can pay if you have the money and win automatically, otherwise you can just fight. If the villager dies or the mission times out you fail the mission.

[b]Always available while negative reputation[/b]
3. Siege (Army): Attempt to destroy the enemy city. Drops reputation greatly. City will respawn with a new ruler at slightly negative status after some time if you win.

[b]Requested missions available while positive reputation:[/b]
4. (Common) Recruit units for me. You have some days to train/recruit X of some particular unit you have already unlocked, where X is the cost of the units in resources plus some profit.
5. (Common) I will pay for large quantity X of stone
6. (Common) Defeat enemy patrols: Defeat all within some timeframe. Causes target reputation loss.
7. (Common) Meet informant. Guards start neutral. A villager is in a downloaded city at a random spot. Breaking or killing anything turns everyone hostile. Talking to this villager also turns all guards hostile. After talking to the villager, escape. Killing guards furthers reputation loss.
8. (Common) Insult. Text mission only. Walk to another city and insult their leader. Player can pick from various insults. Causes reputation loss with that city, but gain with the source city.
9. (Common) Show of force. Same as walk around, but killing enemy units gains reputation for the source city, with more reputation loss/gain for the target and source city respectively for more units killed.

[b]Coming next week[/b]
10. (Rare) Magic contest: Shoot targets rapidly to get to the next round.
11. (Rare) Archery contest: Bet on how far you can get in the contest. You can't move from your starting spot and start with a cracked bow only. Shoot various targets. Success makes new peasants spawn farther away. You only have a limited number of arrows.
12. (Rare) Arena battle: 10 waves of increasingly difficult battles. Enemies keep spawning until you are knocked out. You can place a bet on how far you can get.
Extra mission available while max reputation
13. Court princess: Player can give all gems currently in inventory to the ruler's daughter. Once you reach a certain gold value of gems she agrees to marry you. Shows 1 of 3 custom illustrations. You can marry all 3 daughters, but can only marry each daughter once. Destroying this city resets the love resource, but does not unmarry you if married already.
Positive reputation benefit
City internally keeps track of a gold value of free units to be provided to the player. Each city has an archetype – melee, ranged, or magic that scales with campaign time. Being married doubles the rate of gold increase. Higher reputation also increases gold increase.

notes.title: Campaign army balance patch
notes.content:
[h1]Campaign army balancing overview[/h1]
Certain units are now more effective against other units. Broadly speaking
[list]
[*] Archers beat unshielded units, and especially mages, if engaged at range. You will still need to direct the archers to fire at the mages in commander mode.
[*] Shielded units beat archers of the same level
[*] Mages beat melee units of the same level
[*] Skirmisher type units (goblins) beat melee units of the same level but have low health so die easily if caught
[*] Two handed / high damage units beat units that ressurect or summon other units
[*] Undead beat non-undead of the same type, however undead cannot be saved through leadership
[/list]

[h1]Specific fixes[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Increase goblin damage to be in-line with other units, especially when punching or kicking. Goblins are more likely to dodge as a defensive tactic.
[*] Summoners summon and attack less often, and have a large cooldown between summons
[*] Fix units that can wield multiple weapons using weapon ranges for the weapon they don't currently have equipped
[*] Higher level crossbow shots now do the correct amount of damage
[*] Fix suit of armor giving a lot of gold instead of 1 steel
[*] Increase gold cost to directly buy units vs upgrading them. This is to address leadership seeming to still not be useful enough.
[*] Villages now produce population more slowly. This is to address leadership seeming to still not be useful enough.
[*] Partially fix minotaur attacks, although I may have to redo the minotaur in the future because the attack animation set doesn't work well for the game.
[*] Increase cooldown on necromancer summon so it is possible for high damage units to overwhelm the necromancer
[*] Fix health values for enemy shields
[*] Fix AI units not being able to dodge each other's ranged attacks
[*] Balance enemy female wizard. She can stun knock down units, but is vulnerable to attack from other directions
[*] Fix suit of armor unit equipping wrong shield type
[*] Balance damage, range, accuracy, rate of fire for archer units to normally beat mage units at long range
[*] Tweak damage, health, stamina and mana drain of male wizard
[*] Zombies now leave rot clouds when they die, slowing all units in the area
[*] Improve audio for various units
[*] [b]Meynolt[/b]: Fix commander mode crash
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Fix randomly generated terrain unit unlock quests not available if you had ever played a randomly generated terrain map. A similar bug exists for units unlocked through dungeons.
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Raise dead description now includes 'for a limited time'

[h1]Progress update[/h1]
Fixes are a little slower while most of my effort is currently going towards adding the new cities feature, as described in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/980640/discussions/1/3130541756144344132/]city mission design[/url] post.

[h1]Patch notes[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Increase volume of dungeon music
[*] Fix end of level display stats when dying
[*] Suit of armor now has low resistance to magic damage (increased from none) as it is otherwise easy to get around his shield
[*] The second level boss dungeon now has a greater change for archers to spawn, reducing the effectiveness of hiding on platforms
[*] Limit mage light to 3 instances at once
[*] After completing an order, friendly units will default to following the player rather than standing around
[*] When no units are available to spawn at a spawn point in the dungeon, spawn nothing rather than units that don't fit the current game progression randomly
[*] Fix bug where minimap camera would not show some or all unit icons
[*] Mage light travels a little farther
[*] The mission to rescue villagers from the horde lair has the enemies start aware of the player so at night they don't just stand around unable to see or know where to go
[*] Reduce max dungeon texture memory usage from 3.167 MB to 2.078 MB. This may reduce unexplained GPU related crashes
[*] Fix villagers you are supposed to rescue from dungeons being sunk into the floor
[*] Reduce time until meditate starts to 6 seconds. This is to reduce the effectiveness of kiting.
[*] [b]xxRaIenXX[/b]: Disable pooling objects between scenes. This may fix the purple texture when shooting mana bolts.
[*] [b]Ziprar[/b]: Add XP values tooltip to end of level and level up screen progress bar
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Refactor weapon damage, so that the player can't just dump points in weaponry and kill late game units without challenged. Reduced benefit of AvatarAttributeRank_Weaponry_Bonus from 5% to 3%, Mana bolts ember shard research from 10% to 6%. To offset this and make weaponry an optional rather than required stat, increase increase base weapon damage by 33%, and increase bonus for higher level weapons from 25% to 33%.
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Refactor enemy health, so the player can't outscale late-game enemies. This makes mid and late game enemies noticeably harder and changes the strategy needed to deal with them.  Increase tier 2 unit health so they have about 3X, and tier 3 units so they have about 6X, the health of tier 1 units. Further boost health of undead to reflect the penalty they cannot be knocked out, but always die. Mages and archers still have noticeably less health than melee focused units. Certain spells now do more damage, or more damage at higher levels to counteract the increased health
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Reset player loadout if the loadout is somehow corrupted and overequips items past the limit
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Increase flurry window by 1 second
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Limit blink number of uses per mission and cooldown to reduce exploiting blink to kite enemies
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Blink can now only be used 5 times per mission. This is to prevent kiting enemies forever.
[/olist]

notes.title: Additional story missions unlocked
notes.content:
Request to our players: If you had not previously given Empire of Ember a thumbs-up on Steam, and feel it now deserves one, please help out by leaving a review, or updating your old review. A lot of prior thumbs-down were for launch issues that no longer exist. Once we are mostly positive again I can launch a new marketing push, and the new players will help with continued development.

[h1]Major changes since the last content patch two weeks ago[/h1]
Save files should be compatible, however I strongly recommend starting a new game to take advantage of the economy fixes and to get the new entropy spell for free. You get a certain amount of resources for free by skipping the tutorial so feel free to do so.
[olist]
[*] Most major bugs fixed
[*] You no longer get significant amounts of money from breaking things, the amount of objects in dungeons was massively unbalancing the economy and making it not necessary to trade with villages or train units.
[*] All player attributes reworked so all attributes are now useful. In particular you can't just kite or dodge endlessly, so ranged weapons are actually ranged now.
[*] You can now buy higher level equipment from the market with random probabilities, rather than having to buy all equipment from lowest to highest tier
[*] The bow does much more base damage so missing at long range is no longer punishing. However, headshot damage without abilities is reduced. Combined with not being able to dodge endlessly is now truly a long range weapon as intended.
[*] Player melee attacks now always hit all enemies in range, rather than the first enemy, making it much more powerful
[*] Staffs / Wands heavily rebalanced. They no longer slow down the player when 'reloading' but cannot be 'reloaded' while running or dodging.
[*] Added entropy spell to quickly break items in dungeons
[/olist]
[h1]Minor changes since the last patch on the 28th[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Reduce number of enemies in dungeons
[*] Markets should not sell equipment the player already has
[*] Fixed highlighting a destroyed village just showing a white square
[*] Player can play through additional storyline missions that are fairly difficult
[*] Fix benefice sword
[*] Fix werewolf unit
[*] Updated Post Processing profiles to share consistent effects across all profiles
[*] Fix roaming horde units overspawning
[*] Fix stairs in dungeon requiring player to jump
[*] Fix unit being stuck in getting up state forever when trapped
[*] Reenable tree removal code for AI so they don't spawn on top of trees
[*] Unlocking discovered units now costs spellbooks instead of gold
[*] [b]PotatoTheScourge[/b]: Fix crash caused by going to build mode, then options screen
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Entropy hits units, and kills villagers you are supposed to rescue
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Greatly increase cooldown, increase mana cost, decrease non-upgraded range of blink so it can't be used to kite enemies so easily or without risk
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: From always dropping 3 gold, environmental props have 1/4 chance to drop 1 gold. The reason was that the player could earn over 1000 gold from breaking everything in a dungeon, where the intent was breaking props was a small bonus that would not significantly impact the economy.
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: From always dropping 1 stone/wood/steel have a 1/10th chance to drop 1 from random props. But you always get rewarded from breaking enemy weapons and shields
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Increase pickup radius of gold by 1.95 and pickup radius of other objects by 1.5. This is to make it so you don't have to wait for broken object fragments to disappear before pickup.
[/olist]
[h1]Major changes planned within the next month[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Rework melee combat with better animations and enemy feedback. Currently there is not a good interactive feedback cycle between attacks and blocks, and the animations feel disconnected.
[*] Add custom animations for most spells
[*] Add enemy cities. Some players have complained there isn't enough content. This is because the focus of the game was always meant to be downloading enemy cities. While it is currently in the game it's not in the forefront and easy to find. Most likely enemy cities will send units to attack the player and the player's city, either through diplomacy or simply being always hostile.
[*] More unit sounds. While most unit sounds are currently fine as they come from Ember, they are missing fear sounds or sounds for certain actions.
[*] Localize to Chinese. I hired a professional company to help with this so expect the quality to be fairly good.
[*] Continue to balance gameplay generally. My main concern at this point is the game is too difficult.
[*] Restart marketing effort. I had stopped trying to market the game over the last month while I fixed the bugs and balance issues reported. I'll gauge user feedback but it seems like the recent reviews have all been positive. If this trend continues I'll dig deep and find a marketing company to help us with that.
[/olist]

notes.title: Staff and attribute balancing patch
notes.content:
[h1]Attributes improvement[/h1]

Previously you could outrun all enemies even at level 1 and dodge several times. You also had enough mana to cast most spells several times and could recharge between battles. Athleticism now is a very important stat defensively, as without it you can only dodge once and can't really outrun enemies. You need to put points into willpower if you plan to use magic more than one or twice. The staff doesn't slow you down when on cooldown anymore, but the cooldown resets if you dodge or run (like a regular shooter reload) so you are now very vulnerable with the staff and can't just tank enemies while dodging. 

While you can still focus on particular stats doing so now makes your character unbalanced and vulnerable. This means there's a tradeoff that wasn't really there before. Also the staff isn't automatically the best weapon, it's good for mid-range but leaves you vulnerable close range

[h1]Changelist[/h1]

[olist]
[*] Fix DungeonTile_Stairs not spawning enemies
[*] Fix dungeon boss rooms sometimes not ending due to units on the roof
[*] All melee attacks can now hit multiple targets, to increase the usefulness of melee attacks as well as reduce frustration from hitting walls
[*] Reduce mana cost of push spell
[*] Reduce chance of low level units dropping high level items
[*] Fix necromancer raise dead spell and other errors that caused the necromancer to just stand around instead
[*] Fix stay near allies decision. Previously a unit with nothing else to do would decide to stay near allies too far away and just stand around instead. Applies to healers that want to heal nearby allies.
[*] Reduce slow effect time of mana bolts to 1 seconds. Also show effect when slow effect is active on enemies
[*] Active on AI status effects are now pooled
[*] Fix avatar being able to attack his own city in roam mode
[*] Make blood decals last longer
[*] Reduce shadows too far away to see on forest random map scene in order to improve performance
[*] Summoner fixes: Increase stamina cost to throw flask so he throws less often
[*] Summoner fixes: Fix summoned units not having weapons
[*] Summoner fixes: Fix standing around attempting to summon but not doing so if had a previous target but no current target
[*] Mana bolts recharge times balanced to favor 'reload'
[*] Add shader variants from tutorial, which tend to apply across the whole game
[*] Increase number of enemies in linear mission 2. These are mostly level 1 enemies while the player is level 5-8, so there should be more.
[*] Athleticism improvement: Dodging without improving athleticism now takes nearly all your stamina. Improving athleticism reduces this cost. Running now starts out only 30% faster than walking, but increases as you improve athleticism.
[*] Improve staff: I found it was not fun to suddenly not be able to move effectively if your staff went on cooldown. This was updated so you can still fully walk. However, running, dodging, jumping, casting spells, or not equipping the staff prevents the staff from recharging while you are doing one of those activities. This also indirectly makes willpower more important, because if you cannot shoot you need to rely on your magic. 
[*] Improve staff: Mana bolts no longer cause living enemies to flee on damage.  The rate of fire made it too probable to occur and so the player wouldn't need to defend himself other than by shooting attackers.
[*] Slightly increase spread of mana bolts
[*] Fix trap trigger in dungeon tile 3 way junction
[*] Units in dungeon now roam by default
[*] Fix units staying in place and not attacking if they get up near the edge of a cliff
[*] Double alert radius in dungeons from 4 to 8 meters so units in the same room are less likely to just stand around
[*] Performance: Linear mission 1 limit shadow distance
[*] Fix not checking equipment stash for attribute modifiers
[*] Bosses, including dungeon bosses, should not be able to lose their weapons due to upgraded telekinesis or being knocked down
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: No longer get experience from destroying breakable objects
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Decrease starting mana, currently there isn't much reason to increase willpower as you can just wait for mana to recharge and cast whatever you want.
[*] [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Increase throw fire range
[/olist]

notes.title: Bugs and balance patch

Bug fix updates are slowing down as it's taking increasing effort to find bugs that are less severe. I'll keep looking for bugs as I find them but I'm going to start to transition to improving melee combat and adding enemy cities.

[b]Save file compatibility[/b]
If you haven't started a new game with the last week I suggest doing so, as the economy has been revamped. Also you get the mage light spell free if you start a new game.

[list]
[*] Unlock additional missions and enemies

[*] Enemy audio will be revised / improved over the next 6 weeks
[/list]
[b]Later plans[/b]
[list]
[*] Currently if you defend against a siege a portal to another world opens and you can fight other player's cities. However, I feel that isn't very immersive. Instead, (hostile?) cities will appear on the campaign map at game start. Those cities will send out troops to attack you and villages.

notes.title: Stability and economy update
notes.content:
[list]
[*] General stability: Change walls, buildings fragmentation for player city to use a more memory efficient and better looking fragmentation. This will reduce memory and load times slightly for now, but will improve further as more assets are processed over the coming weeks. The game should also crash less often on lower end computers on the first level.
[*] General stability: Add checks across the project to try to reduce crashes of unknown origin reported by analytics
[*] Try to reduce how often enemies intersect each other
[*] Change to try to fix occupied villages being attacked. This bug would result in you saving the occupied village, only for it to immediately go under siege again
[*] Slightly increase the number of enemies in dungeons generally, but force them to occupy all spawn regions before spawning more than one in a single spawn region. This reduces the problem of large empty rooms followed by another room where you get mobbed
[*] Make dungeon boss rooms have fewer enemies at the same time.
[*] It now takes longer to reach higher player levels
[*] Make easier dungeons even shorter than before, and expose DungeonLengthDifficultyModifier_Easy , etc. to Difficulty_Default.json so it is easier to change in the future.
[*] Thanks to [b]Galdred[/b]: Leadership now gives +2 instead of +1 to your army unit limit.
[*] Thanks to [b]Galdred[/b]: Meditate will now invoke while walking, but be stopped by running, attacking, or taking damage. This is a small change functionally but makes the pacing of the game much more fun.
[*] Thanks to [b]Orgasinator[/b], [b]Darth Trog[/b], [b]Amaltos[/b]: Make player immune to fall damage when starting a new map.
[*] Thanks to [b]Charls Barkly[/b]. Tweak prices of rings, gems, amulets, weapons so you wouldn't be able to get very powerful items early in the game just by buying them, and merchants buy them for less gold.
[*] Thanks to [b]Charls Barkly[/b]. Increase melee damage 20% to better reflect the risk the player takes going into melee.
[*] Thanks to [b]xxRaIenXX[/b]: Revamp unit costs so your focus is on building blacksmiths for higher level units, not on markets, and less economy is spent on upkeep. This is a major change to how the economy works will will need a game restart to evaluate.
[*] Thanks to [b]Orgasinator[/b]: Fix errors after when placing spawn points in build mode
[*] Thanks to [b]Nogitsune[/b]: Skipping the tutorial now gives resources
[*] Thanks to [b]Darth Trog[/b]: Fix location save bug caused by starting a quest associated with a location while in the throne room. This affects any quest you get from your throne room that starts in a city
[*] Thanks to [b]Darth Trog[/b]: The battle to save the village after beating the first linear mission will no longer destroy the village if you kill the attackers instead of run.
[/list]

notes.title: Update 3/6/2021
notes.content:
[olist]
[*] On the army recruitment page, you can now select loadouts for certain units that hold weapons. For example, a two handed weapon vs. a sword and shield.
[*] Enemy and friendly armies on maps that focus on large scale battles now move as a group, in formation
[*] Friendly units on most maps now start out attacking enemies rather than following the player. This is to reduce the number of commands needed for new players and it is less important to always follow the player now that friendly armies move as a group
[*] Design change: Previously units only got experience from completing battles while in your army. Now, units left in town now also gain a small amount of experience per day. This provides the player a safe path to level up units while low on gold, by recruiting low level units then leaving them behind. The UI panel title was renamed from Garrison to Training to indicate to the player that leaving units behind gains them experience. Units in the garrison now take half upkeep rounded up, rather than no upkeep as before, to reflect the benefit of training them.
[*] Design change: Previously it was too random to discover new unit types. This led to the player upgrading his army through normal gameplay to max level, with no apparent further upgrade path. To fix this, unit unlock quests cost gold instead of spellbooks, because the player often does not have spellbooks. Unlocking new unit types through dungeons is now extremely likely to the point that this is the primary way to unlock new unit types. In addition, rewards from dungeon opportunities have better rarity scaling, so you are much less likely to see high-tier objects. This makes researching multiple times more beneficial, and finding a rare object more exciting.
[*] Design change: Previously upgrading the player's tower cost many of all types of resources. Now it simply takes spellbooks and gold. This makes it more clear early in the game what building a library is for, and to provide a benefit to libraries even if the player has no units to research
[*] Design change: Using food as upkeep previously felt like just another form of money and was required to field armies, so was a forced decision rather than an interesting one. Converted the concept of food to population. 1 population is used to recruit each unit and units no longer have food upkeep. This makes lower level worthwhile to keep alive, as it costs a population point to recruit both low and high level units, and provides an incentive to directly recruit higher level units.  The major benefit of farms is now to increase your army limit. You can get more population from villages, putting more play emphasis on trading with villages.
[*] More localization work
[*] AI fighting other AI will now knock each other down if their attack has knockback ability and also reduces the target to zero poise. This is useful for pitchfork farmers, who are designed to play this role when in large groups.
[*] Skipped painting terrain from placed buildings on all maps but the player's city, which greatly improves load times and reduces memory usage for those maps that no longer do so.
[*] Skipped removing trees from terrain when trees intersected spawning AI. This turned out to be an extremely slow operation so I'm just not doing it for now. I might revisit later if it is a problem.
[*] Moved when the AI's behavior tree is loaded, removing the hitch that occurred when the goblins spawn in the first city defense mission.
[*] The player's movement is reduced when the staff charge is depleted and recharging, not only while attempting to fire. This fixes the exploit of being able to kite enemies with impunity, and adds strategy as to when to fully deplete the staff vs. holding fire.
[*] Friendly villages are now more likely to spawn closer to the player's tower. Previously they would spawn at entirely random locations within the biome, making them too hard to find.
[*] In-air blood decals from minor damage to humans are now larger
[*] Units that are holding large shields now attack and move more slowly. Regular sized shields only have a small movement penalty.
[*] Units that are using blunt weapons do about 85% damage to all unit types. Units that are using slash weapons do 100% weapons to living units, and about 66% damage to undead units. This adds strategy to what loadout the player gives to his units.
[*] The player's staff attacks now do less damage, to offset that they rarely miss.
[*] Walls now have 50% more health, to make siege battles last longer
[/olist]

notes.title: Game Update 2/13/2021
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Vines barrels now do low damage over time in addition to rooting their opponents.
[*] Equipment you buy or find is now color coded to indicate rarity
[*] Stamina abilities now cost less to use, but stamina recovers more slowly, to make combat more tactical while also letting players use abilities more often once combat starts
[*] Increase staff total charge so player is less likely to run out of shots against a single enemy. This is balanced by the time to recharge taking longer between enemies.
[*] Added beat tutorial achievement as a placeholder for further achievement work
[*] Removed less helpful autosaves to reduce the number of autosave files. Autosave filenames now also hint at why they were generated.
[*] Increase unit time to forget units so they can reach from their starting positions across long maps
[*] Increase starting spellbooks to 20 to match costs for random events
[*] Increase starting steel to 20 so the player is guaranteed an upgrade option for their first unit upgrade events
[*] Fixed too high level units being selected for enemy spawns from spawn points, meaning enemies in dungeons were often too high level.
[*] Fixed pathfinding in dungeons
[*] The chest in boss rooms in dungeons now gives a good random reward rather than gold
[/list]

notes.title: Gameplay patch 2/11/2021
notes.content:
[list]
[*] At the end of encounters enemies now have a chance to drop loot of varying rarity. Loot can take the form of gemstones to be sold for money, rings or amulets that increase your stats, or rarely rings or amulets that grant special powers.
[*] Gold, aside from dropped loot, is now more scarce, and is more scarce overall. This should make the player have to work for money rather be granted enough to buy a building after every fight.
[*] Food is now dropped from bandit camps, but not every battle
[*] There are now more enemies in bandit lairs, but fewer enemies in roaming battles. This gives the player more options of what difficulty fights to take up
[*] Increased volume of avatar footsteps
[*] The game will no longer make a new autosave immediately after loading a game. This will prevent making multiple of the same autosave when retrying a mission
[*] All mission levels up to mission 3 are now included in the build
[*] Fixed attack decision not correctly calculating priority to targets. Most noticeably enemies are now more likely to attack the player if the player is threatening them
[*] Fix terrain painter making terrain black
[*] Fix spawning units of the wrong type in downloaded cities
[*] Fix units looking in the wrong direction in commander mode
[*] Ranged units with a hold position order whose attacks are blocked will now wait to attack rather than run back and forth
[/list]
